thread:
Maria: Quick sync — I want to propose a different framing for the upcoming packaging work: 'usage lanes' instead of tweaking slabs/credits. The idea is 3 lanes (interactive, background, batch) with per-lane caps and optional per-customer overrides. Goal: simpler dev UX + clearer SLA/billing mapping. Thoughts?

Jake: Sounds promising. Lanes map to different latency/throughput profiles, right? Interactive = low-latency, small tokens; batch = high-throughput, high-token. How do we map models/variants?

Maria: Exactly. Map models by lane via routing rules. Plan is: default lane per route, with a route override. We also need a fallback lane when capacity is constrained.

Sophia: Sales + CSM love clarity. Need to confirm: can customers buy "lane add-ons"? i.e., reserve X qps in interactive lane as an add-on. If not, large customers will ask for per-lane commits.

Olivier: From finance POV we need predictable recognition. Per-lane reserves add complexity but are fine if we treat them like small reserved capacity SKUs. Main ask: define migration path for customers on existing commit model to this lanes model.

Anya: Legal flag — any per-lane commit must be clearly described in contract terms. Also define failure modes: if we throttle a lane, is that a breach or just a performance degradation? We should add explicit outage/latency carveouts for lane-level throttling.

Chris: CS notes — migration friction can be high. Suggest a transitional offer: map existing commits to an "equivalent lane reserve" and include some free trial of interactive lane for 30 days so apps can validate.

Jake: Quick follow-up on implementation: runtime routing already supports request tags and model variants. New pieces:
- config schema for lanes
- routing policy evaluation order (route override > lane reserve > default)
- telemetry per-lane in Console
Example config sketch:
```yaml
lanes:
  interactive:
    max_qps: 120
    default_model: redwood-1.2-lowlat
  background:
    max_qps: 800
    default_model: redwood-1.2-highthru
overrides:
  routes:
    /api/generate-chat: interactive
```

Maria: Nice. We should also define launch criteria: 1) Console UI for lane assignment, 2) Billing SKU/schema, 3) docs + migration guide, 4) 2 pilot customers onboarded and billing captured.

Sophia: Pilot ask: can we run a small pilot with Acme and Nimbus? They requested clearer per-feature QoS. I can get commitment if we offer a 3-month pilot at a discounted lane-reserve rate.

Olivier: Discount ok under a pilot clause but capture expected conversion % in a short doc. Also need to ensure refunds / early-termination math is handled.

Anya: For contracts, propose a short pilot addendum template: defines reserved lane, discount %, metrics to validate success, conversion window. That keeps legal overhead low.

Chris: Ops concerns: lane-level caching & KV usage — background jobs often have long prefixes and will benefit from larger KV caches. We should surface per-lane cache hints to the runtime. Otherwise cost efficiency suffers.

Jake: Agree. We'll add a per-lane cache_budget_hint param. Also want a safe default: if lane reserve exhausted, fallback to a "best-effort" lane that has reduced throughput but preserves tail latency for interactive.

Maria: Important product trade: do we expose explicit per-lane soft-floors (guaranteed) vs soft-caps (best-effort)? My recommendation: offer three modes for each lane on the SKU page — reserved (hard guarantee), prioritized (soft-floor, preemptible), and open (no guarantee).

Sophia: Sales will push for reserved guarantees at scale. Need clear pricing multipliers for reserved vs prioritized. Also need per-customer per-lane ceilings to prevent noisy neighbors.

Olivier: Pricing idea: base price per token by lane \u2014 then multipliers: reserved = x1.8, prioritized = x1.2, open = x1.0. We'll model cost in the worksheet and share.

Anya: Legal — ensure prioritized/reserved definitions include remediation SLA and crediting method. Also require customers to provide traffic shaping info for reserved lanes.

Chris: Operational rollback plan: 1) disable lane overrides globally, 2) fallback to default routing, 3) bill customers based on actual usage in the month of rollback with pro-rated credits if we didn't meet reserved guarantees. Ops happy to own tools for disabling overrides.

Jake: Engineering estimate request: core work (routing + config + telemetry) ~ 3 sprints; console UI + billing wiring + docs + pilot support ~ 2 sprints. Total ~ 5 sprints with 2 engs and 1 PM. Any objections?

Maria: That aligns. Let's set milestones: M1 (spec + legal template + pricing multipliers) by end of next sprint; M2 (runtime + console MVP) end of Q2; M3 (pilot + billing) in early Q3.

Sophia: I'll line up Acme and Nimbus and share pilot expectations doc. :thumbsup:

Olivier: I'll run the pricing sensitivity and send the model.

Anya: Drafting pilot addendum now, will share for review.

Chris: I'll prepare a migration checklist for existing commit customers and a rollout playbook.

Maria: Thanks everyone — I'll turn this into an RFC with the config sketch + launch criteria and tag folks for review.

Jake: Thanks — will add a short perf/latency test plan to the RFC.

Sophia: Will add the pilot contact list.

Olivier: Put the finance model into the RFC as an attachment.

Anya: Ping when legal draft is up.

Chris: Marking action items in CS board.
